topics.description: The public-domain Panchatantra/Hitopadesha fable retold in simple Sanskrit prose: the old heron's lie about the coming fishermen, his daily betrayal of the trusting fish, and the observant crab who sees the heap of bones and destroys the deceiver in self-defence.

topics.name: पतन्ति परपीडकाः — Title and Central Theme
topics.description: The meaning of the title 'those who torment others fall'; the contrast between परोपकार (helping others) and परपीडन (tormenting others); how cruelty and deceit carry the seed of their own destruction.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building senior-secondary Sanskrit vocabulary from the story and verses: words such as सरः, धीवरः, जालम्, चञ्चुः, शिला, अस्थिराशिः, ग्रीवा, दंष्ट्रा, धैर्यम्, अतिलौल्यम्, वृत्तान्तः and their English meanings.

topics.name: नीतिश्लोकाः — Verses on Karma, Ahimsa and the Fall of the Wicked
topics.description: Five authentic public-domain verses — परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्, अहिंसा परमो धर्मः, भक्षयित्वा बहून् मत्स्यान्, यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु, and अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का — with शब्दार्थ, अन्वय, translation and moral.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Lakara
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the chapter: विसर्ग/दीर्घ/यण् सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद; षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, उपपद and नञ् समास with विग्रह; the seven विभक्ति roles with textual examples; and the लट्, लङ्, लृट् and विधिलिङ् लकाराः.

topics.name: Translation and Comprehension
topics.description: Translating the story's prose paragraphs and the नीतिश्लोकाः into simple English, answering comprehension questions on events, motives and morals, and connecting the fable's warning against oppression to modern situations.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: कथा-परिचयः — The Tale of the Heron and the Crab (बक-कर्कट-कथा)
learning_outcomes.description: Recall the sequence of events of the बक-कर्कट-कथा — the heron's feigned grief, the lie about the fishermen, the rock and the bone-heap, and the crab's counter-stroke — and identify its characters.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: पतन्ति परपीडकाः — Title and Central Theme
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of the title पतन्ति परपीडकाः and the central contrast between परोपकार and परपीडन, and show how the story justifies the title.
Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of Sanskrit words drawn from the story and verses, and supply the correct Sanskrit word for a given English meaning.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: नीतिश्लोकाः — Verses on Karma, Ahimsa and the Fall of the Wicked
learning_outcomes.description: Recite and explain the five नीतिश्लोकाः of the chapter with their अन्वय, word meanings and morals — Vyasa's two sayings, the supremacy of अहिंसा, the greedy heron, karma finding its doer, and the danger of excess.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: पतन्ति परपीडकाः — Title and Central Theme
learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the moral questions of the chapter — why the fish were deceived, why the crab's act is self-defence and not परपीडन, what the bone-heap symbolises — and apply the lesson to modern situations of fraud and oppression.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Lakara
learning_outcomes.description: Perform सन्धि-विच्छेद of joined forms from the chapter (धर्मस्तथाहिंसा, बलिर्बद्धः, कर्तारमनुगच्छति) and give the विग्रह and type of compounds such as परपीडकः, परोपकारः, अस्थिराशिः and अहिंसा.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Lakara
learning_outcomes.description: Identify the विभक्ति and number of nouns and the लकार (लट्, लङ्, लृट्, विधिलिङ्) of verbs occurring in the chapter, and state the grammatical role each form plays in its sentence.
Translate prose passages and verses of the chapter into simple English and answer comprehension questions on their words, grammar and meaning.

chapter_summary.title: पतन्ति परपीडकाः (Patanti Parapidakah) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 10: the fable of the cruel heron and the crab (बक-कर्कट-कथा), the meaning of the title 'those who torment others fall', five नीतिश्लोकाः on ahimsa, karma and the fate of the wicked, and the grammar — सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति, लकार — drawn from the text.

branches.label: कथा — बकः कर्कटकश्च
details: Old heron feigns grief, invents fishermen-lie
Carries fish 'to safety', eats them on a rock
Crab sees bone-heap, grips heron's neck

branches.label: शीर्षकार्थः — Theme
details: Cruelty carries the seed of its own ruin

branches.label: नीतिश्लोकाः — Key verses
details: अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का — avoid all excess

branches.label: मूल्यानि — Values
details: Never trust sweet words without proof

branches.label: व्याकरणम् — Grammar
details: लकार: पतन्ति लट्, अपतत् लङ्, नेष्यामि लृट्

sections.heading: The title and the theme
bullets: पतन्ति परपीडकाः means 'those who torment others fall' — परपीडकः is one who gives pain (पीडा) to others (पर).
Vyasa's summary of all dharma frames the chapter: परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् — helping others earns merit, harming them earns sin.
Sanskrit fable literature teaches that deceit devours the deceiver: the pit dug for others swallows the digger himself.

sections.heading: The story: the heron's deceit
bullets: An old heron, too weak to catch fish, decides to live by trickery (उपाय) instead of strength.
He feigns grief and tells the fish that fishermen will come the next day, cast nets and kill every water-creature.
Offering to carry them one by one (एकैकशः) to a safe lake, he wins the blind trust of the frightened creatures.
Daily he flies each batch of fish to a huge rock and devours them; a great heap of bones (अस्थिराशिः) piles up.

sections.heading: The story: the crab's counter-stroke
bullets: The crab asks to be carried too; the heron, greedy for a new taste, places him on his neck and flies to the rock.
Looking down, the crab sees the bone-heap and instantly understands the whole deceit and his own danger.
Keeping his courage — आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम् — he grips the heron's neck with his sharp pincers and kills him.
Returning, he reports everything; the creatures praise his intelligence and become fearless — the oppressor has fallen.

sections.heading: The verses on ahimsa, karma and excess
bullets: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः... — non-injury is the highest dharma, self-control, charity and austerity all at once.
भक्षयित्वा बहून् मत्स्यान्... — the traditional verse of this very tale: out of excessive greed (अतिलौल्यात्) the heron died in the crab's grip.
यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु... — as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, a past deed unerringly follows its doer (कर्म कर्तारम् अनुगच्छति).
अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का... — excess destroyed Lanka (arrogance), the Kauravas (pride) and bound Bali (even giving); avoid excess everywhere.

sections.heading: Grammar from the text
bullets: सन्धि-विच्छेद: धर्मस्तथाहिंसा = धर्मः + तथा + अहिंसा; बलिर्बद्धः = बलिः + बद्धः; कर्तारमनुगच्छति = कर्तारम् + अनुगच्छति; नास्ति = न + अस्ति.
समास: परपीडकः = परेषां पीडकः and परोपकारः = परेषाम् उपकारः (both षष्ठीतत्पुरुष); जलचरः = जले चरति इति (उपपद); अहिंसा = न हिंसा (नञ्).
विभक्ति: पुण्याय / पापाय are चतुर्थी of purpose (तादर्थ्ये); सरसि, शिलायाम्, धेनुसहस्रेषु are सप्तमी; अतिलौल्यात्, कर्कटकग्रहात् are पञ्चमी.
लकार: पतन्ति, विन्दति (लट् present); अवदत्, अपतत् (लङ् past); आगमिष्यन्ति, नेष्यामि (लृट् future); वर्जयेत्, भवेत् (विधिलिङ्).

key_takeaways: पतन्ति परपीडकाः — those who torment others fall; the heron perished by the fruit of his own cruelty, not by any outside power.
Vyasa's essence of all the Puranas: परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् — help earns merit, harm earns sin.
अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-injury stands at the summit of dharma, self-control, charity and austerity.
Karma is unerring: like a calf finding its mother among a thousand cows, a deed always finds its doer.
Excess of anything — pride, arrogance, greed, even giving — precedes a fall: अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्.
Do not trust sweet words without verification; the fish died of blind trust, the crab lived by observation and courage (आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम्).
From the text: विसर्ग/दीर्घ सन्धि (धर्मस्तथाहिंसा), षष्ठीतत्पुरुष समास (परपीडकः = परेषां पीडकः), चतुर्थी of purpose (पुण्याय), and the four लकाराः लट्, लङ्, लृट्, विधिलिङ्.

glossary.definition: One who torments others (परेषां पीडकः, षष्ठीतत्पुरुष); the oppressor whose fall the chapter's title announces.
Doing good to others (परेषाम् उपकारः); in Vyasa's verse the one root of all merit (पुण्य).
The act of tormenting others; in Vyasa's verse the one root of all sin (पाप).
Non-injury, non-violence (न हिंसा, नञ्समास); declared the highest dharma, self-control, charity and austerity.
Heron or crane; in the fable the old, cunning oppressor who eats the fish he promised to save.
Crab; the observant, courageous creature who sees through the deceit and destroys the heron in self-defence.
Fisherman; the heron's invented threat — 'fishermen will come tomorrow and cast nets' — that frightened the fish.
Heap of bones (अस्थ्नां राशिः); the pile on the rock that exposed the heron's cruelty to the crab.
Excessive greed; the traditional verse says the heron died अतिलौल्यात् — from over-greed — in the crab's grip.
Action and its inevitable fruit; a past deed follows its doer as surely as a calf finds its mother.
Courage, fortitude; the crab's watchword — आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम्, in danger courage alone is strength.
Neck; the heron carried the crab on his neck, and by that same neck the crab destroyed him.
Pincer, claw or fang; the crab's sharp pincers (दंष्ट्रे) were the instrument of the oppressor's fall.
A water-creature (जले चरति इति, उपपदसमास) — the fish, frogs and crabs of the lake.
The Sanskrit potential/optative mood expressing 'should/ought', e.g. वर्जयेत् 'one should avoid'.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — पतन्ति परपीडकाः (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 10)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the story and the नीतिश्लोकाः of the lesson where needed.

questions.question: कथायां वृद्धः बकः मत्स्यान् ग्रहीतुं किमर्थम् असमर्थः अभवत्? (Why had the old heron become unable to catch fish?)
questions.explanation: The heron had grown weak with old age (वार्धक्येन दुर्बलः) and so could no longer hunt by strength — which is why he turned to deceit.

questions.question: 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्' — अनुसारं पापाय किं भवति? (According to the verse, what leads to sin?)
questions.explanation: Vyasa's pair of sayings: helping others (परोपकारः) leads to merit; tormenting others (परपीडनम्) leads to sin.

questions.question: True or False: कर्कटकस्य बकहननम् आत्मरक्षा आसीत्, न तु परपीडनम्। (The crab's killing of the heron was self-defence, not oppression.)
questions.explanation: The crab struck only when his own destruction was imminent; acting to save one's life from an aggressor is आत्मरक्षा, not परपीडन.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — अहिंसा परमो ______। (Fill in the blank with the correct Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: The celebrated verse reads अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-injury is the highest dharma.

questions.question: 'पतन्ति परपीडकाः' इति शीर्षकस्य अर्थं लिखत। कथा शीर्षकं कथं समर्थयति? (Write the meaning of the title and state how the story justifies it.)
questions.answer: The title means 'those who torment others fall'. The heron tormented the trusting water-creatures — deceiving and devouring them — and in the end perished in the grip of the crab, one of his intended victims. His fall came from his own cruelty, proving that oppressors are destroyed by their own deeds.
questions.explanation: पतन्ति = they fall; परपीडकाः = tormentors of others. The heron's death is the story's demonstration of the title.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत — (i) धर्मस्तथाहिंसा (ii) बलिर्बद्धः (iii) कर्तारमनुगच्छति। (Split the sandhi in each form and name the sandhi where possible.)
questions.answer: (i) धर्मस्तथाहिंसा = धर्मः + तथा + अहिंसा (विसर्गसन्धि: ः → स्; दीर्घसन्धि: आ + अ = आ)। (ii) बलिर्बद्धः = बलिः + बद्धः (विसर्गसन्धि — visarga becomes र् before a voiced consonant)। (iii) कर्तारमनुगच्छति = कर्तारम् + अनुगच्छति (म् joins the following vowel).
questions.explanation: All three forms occur in the chapter's verses; splitting them back is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: 'यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम्' — अस्य श्लोकस्य उपमां स्पष्टीकुरुत। (Explain the simile of this verse.)
questions.answer: Just as a calf, released among a thousand cows, unerringly finds its own mother, so a deed done in the past (पूर्वकृतं कर्म) unfailingly follows and finds its doer (कर्तारम् अनुगच्छति). The simile teaches that karma never misses its target — the heron's cruel deeds found him even in the sky.
questions.explanation: The calf-mother simile illustrates the infallibility of the law of karma.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'शिलायाः समीपं गत्वा कर्कटकः अधः अपश्यत्। तत्र अस्थिराशिं दृष्ट्वा सः सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् अवगतवान्। ... सः स्वतीक्ष्णाभ्यां दंष्ट्राभ्यां बकस्य ग्रीवां दृढं गृहीत्वा अपीडयत्।'
(i) कर्कटकः किं दृष्ट्वा सत्यम् अवगतवान्? (ii) 'ग्रीवाम्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (iii) कर्कटकः बकं केन साधनेन अमारयत्? (iv) Translate: 'तत्र अस्थिराशिं दृष्ट्वा सः सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् अवगतवान्।'
questions.answer: (i) कर्कटकः शिलायाम् अस्थिराशिं दृष्ट्वा सत्यम् अवगतवान् — he understood on seeing the heap of bones. (ii) 'ग्रीवाम्' — द्वितीया विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् (object of गृहीत्वा). (iii) सः स्वतीक्ष्णाभ्यां दंष्ट्राभ्यां — with his two sharp pincers. (iv) 'Seeing the heap of bones there, he understood the whole account.'
questions.explanation: The climax passage tests story comprehension, vibhakti recognition and translation together.

questions.question: बक-कर्कट-कथां स्वभाषया लिखत, अन्ते च कथायाः नीतिं स्पष्टीकुरुत। (Narrate the heron-and-crab story in your own words — Sanskrit or English — and state its moral clearly.)
questions.answer: Model answer: An old heron by a great lake, too weak to hunt, feigned grief and told the water-creatures that fishermen would come the next day and kill them all. Offering to carry them one by one to a safe lake, he won their trust — but each day he flew the fish to a huge rock and ate them, until a heap of bones rose there. One day he carried the crab, wanting a new taste. Nearing the rock, the crab saw the bone-heap, understood the deceit, kept his courage and gripped the heron's neck with his sharp pincers until the wicked bird died and fell. The crab returned and told all; the creatures became fearless. Moral: यः परान् पीडयति सः स्वयमेव नश्यति — पतन्ति परपीडकाः; the tormentor of others is destroyed by his own cruelty, while presence of mind and courage protect the innocent.
questions.explanation: Full marks require the complete sequence of events and an explicit statement of the moral.

questions.question: अध्यायस्य पञ्च नीतिश्लोकाः मिलित्वा किं सन्देशं ददति? कर्म-अहिंसा-अति इति त्रयाणां विषयाणाम् आधारेण विस्तरेण लिखत। (What collective message do the five verses of the chapter give? Discuss with reference to karma, ahimsa and excess.)
questions.answer: Model answer: Together the verses build one argument. Vyasa's couplet lays the foundation: all merit flows from helping others, all sin from harming them. The ahimsa verse raises non-injury to the summit of dharma, self-control, charity and austerity — harming others is thus the deepest wrong. The heron-verse (भक्षयित्वा बहून् मत्स्यान्...) shows the law in action: excessive greed delivered the tormentor to death in his victim's grip. The calf-and-mother verse explains why the wicked cannot escape: a past deed follows its doer as unerringly as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows. Finally अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का widens the warning — excess of arrogance destroyed Lanka, pride the Kauravas, and even excess of giving bound Bali — so one should avoid all excess. The collective message: practise अहिंसा and परोपकार, shun harm and excess, for karma unfailingly brings the oppressor down — पतन्ति परपीडकाः.
questions.explanation: The five verses move from principle (merit/sin, ahimsa) through example (the heron) to law (karma) and general warning (excess).

questions.question: कथायां वृद्धः बकः कुत्र अवसत्? (Where did the old heron live?)
questions.explanation: The story opens: तस्य सरसः तीरे एकः वृद्धः बकः अवसत् — the old heron lived on the bank of the lake.

questions.question: बकः मत्स्यान् ग्रहीतुं केन कारणेन असमर्थः अभवत्? (For what reason had the heron become unable to catch fish?)
questions.explanation: सः वार्धक्येन दुर्बलः सन् मत्स्यान् ग्रहीतुम् असमर्थः अभवत् — weakness of old age made hunting impossible.

questions.question: बकः जलचरेभ्यः कां मिथ्यावार्ताम् अकथयत्? (What false news did the heron tell the water-creatures?)
questions.explanation: His lie was that fishermen (धीवराः) would come the next day, cast nets and kill all the water-creatures.

questions.question: बकः मत्स्यान् नीत्वा कुत्र खादति स्म? (Where did the heron take the fish and eat them?)
questions.explanation: He carried them to a huge rock (विशाला शिला) and devoured them there — never to any new lake.

questions.question: कर्कटकः किं दृष्ट्वा बकस्य कपटम् अवगतवान्? (Seeing what did the crab understand the heron's deceit?)
questions.explanation: Looking down at the rock the crab saw the heap of bones (अस्थिराशिः) of the eaten fish and understood everything.

questions.question: कर्कटकः बकं कथम् अमारयत्? (How did the crab kill the heron?)
questions.explanation: He gripped and squeezed the heron's neck firmly with his two sharp pincers (स्वतीक्ष्णाभ्यां दंष्ट्राभ्याम्).

questions.question: कथान्ते कः सरः प्रत्यागत्य सर्वं वृत्तान्तं जलचरेभ्यः न्यवेदयत्? (At the end, who returned to the lake and reported the whole account?)
questions.explanation: The crab slowly returned to his own lake and told the water-creatures everything that had happened.

questions.question: बकः कर्कटकं कुत्र निधाय अनयत्? (Where did the heron place the crab while carrying him?)
questions.explanation: सः कर्कटकं ग्रीवायां निधाय... — he placed the crab on his neck, which later proved fatal to him.

questions.question: बक-कर्कट-कथा कस्याः कथापरम्परायाः प्रसिद्धा कथा अस्ति? (The heron-and-crab tale belongs to which famous story tradition?)
questions.explanation: बक-कर्कट-कथा is a classic fable of the Panchatantra / Hitopadesha nīti-kathā tradition.

questions.question: बकः कर्कटकं नेतुं किमर्थम् अङ्गीकृतवान्? (Why did the heron agree to carry the crab?)
questions.explanation: He thought: 'Long have I eaten fish-flesh; today I shall taste crab-flesh' (अद्य कर्कटकमांसं खादिष्यामि) — greed for a new taste.

questions.question: 'पतन्ति परपीडकाः' इति शीर्षकस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of the title?)
questions.explanation: पतन्ति = they fall; परपीडकाः = tormentors of others — oppressors are destroyed by their own deeds.

questions.question: अध्यायस्य केन्द्रीयः भावः कः? (What is the central theme of the chapter?)
options: The downfall of oppressors through their own cruelty
The victory of physical strength over intelligence
The importance of wealth in life
questions.answer: The downfall of oppressors through their own cruelty
questions.explanation: The chapter's fable and verses all demonstrate that cruelty carries the seed of its own destruction.

questions.question: कथायां बकः कस्य प्रतीकः अस्ति? (In the tale, of whom is the heron a symbol?)
questions.explanation: The heron represents the deceitful oppressor (कपटी परपीडकः) who exploits the trust of the weak.

questions.question: 'परपीडकः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What does the word परपीडकः mean?)
questions.explanation: परान् पीडयति इति परपीडकः — he who gives pain (पीडा) to others (पर).

questions.question: अध्यायानुसारं परोपकारस्य परपीडनस्य च कः विरोधः? (According to the chapter, what is the contrast between paropakara and parapidana?)
questions.explanation: Vyasa's verse states the contrast: helping others leads to merit, tormenting others to sin.

questions.question: 'सरः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of the word सरः?)
questions.explanation: सरः (neuter, सरस्-शब्द) means a lake or pond — the home of the fish and the crab in the story.

questions.question: 'धीवरः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of धीवरः?)
questions.explanation: धीवरः means a fisherman — the heron's invented threat to frighten the water-creatures.

questions.question: 'चञ्चुः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of चञ्चुः?)
questions.explanation: चञ्चुः means beak; the heron picked up fish in his beak (चञ्च्वा गृहीत्वा).

questions.question: 'ग्रीवा' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of ग्रीवा?)
questions.explanation: ग्रीवा means neck — the crab gripped the heron's neck (ग्रीवाम्) with his pincers.

questions.question: 'अस्थि' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of अस्थि?)
questions.explanation: अस्थि (neuter) means bone; the heap of bones (अस्थिराशिः) exposed the heron's deceit.

questions.question: 'धूर्तः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of धूर्तः?)
questions.explanation: धूर्तः means a cunning rogue or cheat — the crab calls the heron अयं धूर्तः on seeing the bones.

questions.question: 'वार्धक्यम्' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of वार्धक्यम्?)
questions.explanation: वार्धक्यम् means old age; the heron was weakened by it (वार्धक्येन दुर्बलः).

questions.question: 'क्षुधा' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of क्षुधा?)
questions.explanation: क्षुधा means hunger; the heron was tormented by hunger (क्षुधया पीडितः).

questions.question: 'जलचरः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of जलचरः?)
options: A creature that moves in water
A bird that flies in the sky
An animal that lives in the forest
A creature that burrows in the earth
questions.answer: A creature that moves in water
questions.explanation: जले चरति इति जलचरः — a water-creature; here the fish, frogs and crabs of the lake.

questions.question: 'एकैकशः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of एकैकशः?)
questions.explanation: एकैकशः means 'one by one' — the heron promised to carry the creatures one at a time.

questions.question: 'शिला' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of शिला?)
questions.explanation: शिला means a rock; the heron ate the fish on a huge rock (विशाला शिला).

questions.question: 'वृत्तान्तः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of वृत्तान्तः?)
questions.explanation: वृत्तान्तः means an account or report of what happened; the crab reported सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् to the creatures.

questions.question: 'निर्भयः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of निर्भयः?)
questions.explanation: निर्भयः = free from fear; with the heron's death the water-creatures became fearless (निर्भयाः अभवन्).

questions.question: 'Net' इत्यस्य कृते संस्कृतपदं किम्? (Which Sanskrit word means 'net'?)
questions.explanation: जालम् means net (धीवराः जालानि क्षेप्स्यन्ति); note the contrast with जलम् 'water'.

questions.question: 'दंष्ट्रा' इति पदस्य कथायां कः अर्थः? (In the story, what does दंष्ट्रा mean?)
questions.explanation: दंष्ट्रा usually means fang; for the crab it denotes his sharp pincers (स्वतीक्ष्णाभ्यां दंष्ट्राभ्याम्).

questions.question: 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्' — इदं वचनद्वयं कस्य इति श्लोके उक्तम्? (According to the verse, whose pair of sayings is this?)
questions.explanation: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् — the verse attributes this two-fold teaching to sage Vyasa.

questions.question: व्यासस्य वचनद्वयं कुत्र सारभूतम् इति श्लोकः वदति? (The verse says Vyasa's two sayings are the essence of what?)
questions.explanation: अष्टादशपुराणेषु — in all the eighteen Puranas, Vyasa's teaching is condensed into this one pair of sayings.

questions.question: श्लोकानुसारं परमो धर्मः कः? (According to the verse, what is the highest dharma?)
questions.explanation: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-injury is declared the highest righteousness.

questions.question: 'अहिंसा' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does अहिंसा mean?)
questions.explanation: अहिंसा = न हिंसा — abstaining from injury or violence toward all creatures.

questions.question: 'भक्षयित्वा बहून् मत्स्यान्...' श्लोकानुसारं बकः कस्मात् कारणात् मृतः? (According to the verse, from what cause did the heron die?)
questions.explanation: अतिलौल्याद् बकः कश्चिद् मृतः कर्कटकग्रहात् — out of excessive greed he died in the crab's grip.

questions.question: 'कर्कटकग्रहात्' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What does कर्कटकग्रहात् mean?)
options: From the grip of the crab
In the house of the crab
For the sake of the crab
With the friendship of the crab
questions.answer: From the grip of the crab
questions.explanation: कर्कटकग्रहात् (पञ्चमी) = from the grasp/grip (ग्रह) of the crab — the cause of the heron's death.

questions.question: 'उत्तमाधममध्यमान्' इति विशेषणं कान् वर्णयति? (Whom does the adjective उत्तमाधममध्यमान् describe?)
options: भक्षितान् मत्स्यान् — the best, worst and middling fish
questions.answer: भक्षितान् मत्स्यान् — the best, worst and middling fish
questions.explanation: The heron devoured many fish of every grade — उत्तम (best), अधम (worst) and मध्यम (middling).

questions.question: 'यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु...' श्लोके वत्सः केषु मध्ये मातरं विन्दति? (In the verse, among what does the calf find its mother?)
questions.explanation: यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् — among a thousand cows the calf finds its own mother.

questions.question: तस्मिन् एव श्लोके पूर्वकृतं कर्म कम् अनुगच्छति? (In that verse, whom does a deed done in the past follow?)
questions.explanation: तथा पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारम् अनुगच्छति — the past deed follows its doer (कर्तारम्).

questions.question: 'अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का' — लङ्का केन कारणेन हता? (By what cause was Lanka destroyed?)
questions.explanation: Lanka fell through excessive arrogance (अतिदर्प) — Ravana's pride destroyed his golden city.

questions.question: 'अतिदाने बलिर्बद्धः' — अतिदानेन कः बद्धः? (Who was bound because of excessive giving?)
questions.explanation: King Bali was bound (by Vamana) through excess of giving — even a virtue in excess brings a fall.

questions.question: 'अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्' — अनेन किम् उपदिश्यते? (What does this line teach?)
questions.explanation: अति = excess; सर्वत्र = everywhere; वर्जयेत् = one should avoid — moderation in all things.

questions.question: कः श्लोकः साक्षात् बक-कर्कट-कथायाः सारं वदति? (Which verse directly summarises the heron-and-crab story?)
options: अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का अतिमाने च कौरवाः...
questions.explanation: That verse names the heron, the devoured fish and death in the crab's grip — the traditional summary of this very fable.

questions.question: अहिंसा-श्लोकानुसारं परमं दानं किम्? (According to the ahimsa verse, what is the highest charity?)
questions.explanation: अहिंसा परमं दानम् — non-injury itself is the highest gift one can give to creatures.

questions.question: कर्कटकस्य बकहननं परपीडनं न मन्यते — किमर्थम्? (Why is the crab's killing of the heron not counted as parapidana?)
options: It was self-defence against imminent destruction
The crab was stronger than the heron
The heron was already dying of old age
questions.answer: It was self-defence against imminent destruction
questions.explanation: The crab struck only when his own death was certain — आत्मरक्षा (self-defence) against an aggressor is not tormenting others.

questions.question: मत्स्यानां विनाशस्य मुख्यं कारणं किम् आसीत्? (What was the chief cause of the fishes' destruction?)
questions.explanation: They trusted the heron's sweet words blindly, without any verification — blind trust (मूढविश्वासः) delivered them to the deceiver.

questions.question: कर्कटकं कः गुणः अरक्षत्? (Which quality saved the crab?)
questions.explanation: Sharp observation (he looked down and saw the bones) and courage in danger (आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम्) saved him.

questions.question: कथा अस्मान् मुख्यतः कस्मात् सावधानान् करोति? (Against what does the story chiefly warn us?)
options: Trusting the sweet words of the wicked without proof
Helping the old and the weak
questions.answer: Trusting the sweet words of the wicked without proof
questions.explanation: The fish perished because they believed the rogue's honeyed assurance without testing it.

questions.question: आधुनिकजीवने 'बकवृत्तिः' कस्मिन् दृश्यते? (In modern life, where is the 'heron's way' most clearly seen?)
options: In a fraudster who promises safety or profit to cheat the trusting
In a doctor who treats patients honestly
In a teacher who corrects student errors
In a farmer who waters his fields daily
questions.answer: In a fraudster who promises safety or profit to cheat the trusting
questions.explanation: Like the heron, the modern fraudster wins trust with false promises of protection or gain, then devours his victims' wealth.

questions.question: Which English proverb best matches the theme of the chapter?
options: He who digs a pit for others falls into it himself
A stitch in time saves nine
Make hay while the sun shines
questions.answer: He who digs a pit for others falls into it himself
questions.explanation: The heron prepared destruction for others and met that very destruction — the pit-digger's fate.

questions.question: बकस्य विनाशस्य वास्तविकं कारणं किम् इति युक्तं मूल्याङ्कनम्? (What is the correct evaluation of the real cause of the heron's destruction?)
questions.explanation: No external enemy destroyed him; his own परपीडन and अतिलौल्य carried him to the rock and to death.

questions.question: अस्थिराशिः कथायां कस्य प्रतीकः? (What does the heap of bones symbolise in the story?)
options: The hidden record of the oppressor's crimes that finally exposes him
The wealth gathered by the heron honestly
questions.answer: The hidden record of the oppressor's crimes that finally exposes him
questions.explanation: Every crime left its trace; the accumulated bones became the evidence that revealed the heron's cruelty to the crab.

questions.question: 'धर्मस्तथाहिंसा' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः? (What is the sandhi-split of धर्मस्तथाहिंसा?)
questions.explanation: The visarga of धर्मः becomes स् before त (विसर्गसन्धि), and तथा + अहिंसा join by दीर्घसन्धि (आ + अ = आ).

questions.question: 'तथाहिंसा' (तथा + अहिंसा) इत्यत्र कः सन्धिः? (Which sandhi operates in तथा + अहिंसा = तथाहिंसा?)
questions.explanation: आ + अ merge into the single long आ — the savarna-dīrgha sandhi.

questions.question: 'कर्तारमनुगच्छति' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः? (What is the split of कर्तारमनुगच्छति?)
questions.explanation: The final म् of कर्तारम् joins the following vowel अ of अनुगच्छति.

questions.question: 'बलिर्बद्धः' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः? (What is the split of बलिर्बद्धः?)
questions.explanation: विसर्गसन्धि: the visarga of बलिः becomes र् before the voiced consonant ब् (रेफादेश).

questions.question: 'नास्ति' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः? (What is the split of नास्ति?)
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घसन्धि): न + अस्ति = नास्ति, 'there is not'.

questions.question: 'परपीडकः' इति पदे कः समासः? (Which compound is परपीडकः?)
questions.explanation: विग्रह: परेषां पीडकः — 'tormentor OF others', a genitive tatpurusha.

questions.question: 'अहिंसा' इति पदे कः समासः? (Which compound is अहिंसा?)
questions.explanation: अहिंसा = न हिंसा — the negative particle नञ् compounded with हिंसा gives 'non-injury'.

questions.question: 'परोपकारः' इत्यस्य समास-विग्रहः कः? (What is the vigraha of परोपकारः?)
questions.explanation: परोपकारः is a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष: 'help OF/TO others' — परेषाम् उपकारः.

questions.question: 'अस्थिराशिः' इत्यस्य समास-विग्रहः कः? (What is the vigraha of अस्थिराशिः?)
questions.explanation: अस्थिराशिः = 'heap OF bones' — genitive tatpurusha with the genitive plural अस्थ्नाम्.

questions.question: 'पतन्ति' इति क्रियापदे कः लकारः किं वचनं च? (What is the lakara and number of पतन्ति?)
questions.explanation: पतन्ति = '(they) fall' — present tense (लट्), third person (प्रथमपुरुष), plural.

questions.question: 'मारयिष्यन्ति' इति क्रियापदे कः लकारः? (What is the lakara of मारयिष्यन्ति?)
questions.explanation: मारयिष्यन्ति = 'they will kill' — simple future (लृट्), marked by the -इष्य- element.

questions.question: 'अपतत्' इति क्रियापदे कः लकारः? (What is the lakara of अपतत्?)
questions.explanation: अपतत् = '(he) fell' — past tense (लङ्), with the augment अ- and ending -त्.

questions.question: 'वर्जयेत्' इति क्रियापदे कः लकारः? (What is the lakara of वर्जयेत्?)
questions.explanation: वर्जयेत् = 'one should avoid' — the optative/potential mood (विधिलिङ्) expressing 'should/ought'.

questions.question: 'नेष्यामि' इति क्रियापदे कः लकारः कः पुरुषः च? (What is the lakara and person of नेष्यामि?)
questions.explanation: नेष्यामि = 'I shall carry' (नी + स्य + मि) — future tense, first person (उत्तमपुरुष) singular.

questions.question: 'सरसि' इति पदे का विभक्तिः किं वचनं च? (What is the vibhakti and number of सरसि?)
questions.explanation: तस्मिन् सरसि = 'IN that lake' — locative (सप्तमी) singular of the neuter सरस्-शब्द.

questions.question: 'वार्धक्येन' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (What is the vibhakti of वार्धक्येन?)
questions.explanation: वार्धक्येन दुर्बलः = 'weak BY/BECAUSE OF old age' — instrumental (तृतीया) expressing cause.

questions.question: 'बकस्य' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (What is the vibhakti of बकस्य?)
questions.explanation: बकस्य ग्रीवाम् = 'the neck OF the heron' — genitive (षष्ठी) singular.

questions.question: 'परोपकारः पुण्याय' इत्यत्र 'पुण्याय' इति पदे का विभक्तिः केन भावेन च? (What vibhakti is पुण्याय, and in what sense?)
questions.explanation: पुण्याय and पापाय are dative (चतुर्थी) of purpose/result: paropakara is FOR (i.e. results in) merit.

questions.question: 'ग्रीवाम्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (What is the vibhakti of ग्रीवाम्?)
questions.explanation: ग्रीवां गृहीत्वा = 'having seized the NECK' — accusative (द्वितीया) singular, the object of the action.

questions.question: 'अतिलौल्यात्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः केन भावेन च? (What vibhakti is अतिलौल्यात्, and in what sense?)
questions.explanation: The ablative (पञ्चमी) here expresses cause: the heron died FROM/BECAUSE OF excessive greed.

questions.question: 'आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम्' — अस्य वाक्यस्य शुद्धः अनुवादः कः? (Which is the correct translation of this sentence?)
options: In times of danger, courage alone is strength
In good times, wealth alone is strength
Strength is dangerous in all times
questions.answer: In times of danger, courage alone is strength
questions.explanation: आपत्काले = in the time of calamity; धैर्यम् एव = courage alone; बलम् = (is) strength — the crab's watchword.

questions.question: 'मूढाः जलचराः तस्य वचने विश्वासं कृतवन्तः' — शुद्धः अनुवादः कः? (Which is the correct translation?)
options: The foolish water-creatures placed their trust in his words
The wise water-creatures doubted his words
The foolish water-creatures attacked him for his words
questions.answer: The foolish water-creatures placed their trust in his words
questions.explanation: मूढाः = foolish; तस्य वचने = in his words; विश्वासं कृतवन्तः = placed trust.

questions.question: 'क्षुधया पीडितः सः चिन्तयामास' — शुद्धः अनुवादः कः? (Which is the correct translation?)
questions.explanation: क्षुधया = by hunger (तृतीया); पीडितः = tormented; चिन्तयामास = thought/reflected (periphrastic perfect).

questions.question: True or False: बकः वस्तुतः जलचरान् नूतनं सरः अनयत्। (The heron actually carried the water-creatures to a new lake.)
questions.explanation: He never took them to any lake; he flew each batch to a huge rock and ate them there.

questions.question: True or False: कर्कटकः शिलायाम् अस्थिराशिं दृष्ट्वा बकस्य कपटम् अवगतवान्। (The crab understood the heron's deceit on seeing the bone-heap on the rock.)
questions.explanation: Looking down at the rock, the crab saw the heap of fish-bones and grasped the whole truth.

questions.question: True or False: बकः वार्धक्येन मृतः। (The heron died of old age.)
questions.explanation: He died in the crab's grip — his neck squeezed by the crab's pincers — not of old age.

questions.question: True or False: कथान्ते कर्कटकः जलचरेभ्यः किमपि न अकथयत्। (At the end, the crab told the water-creatures nothing.)
questions.explanation: He returned to the lake and reported the whole account (सर्वं वृत्तान्तं न्यवेदयत्) to the creatures.

questions.question: True or False: 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्' इति व्यासस्य वचनम् इति श्लोके उक्तम्। (The verse attributes this saying to Vyasa.)
questions.explanation: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् — the verse presents it as Vyasa's two-fold teaching from the eighteen Puranas.

questions.question: True or False: 'यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु...' श्लोकानुसारं पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारं कदापि न प्राप्नोति। (According to the verse, a past deed never reaches its doer.)
questions.explanation: The verse says the opposite: as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, a past deed unfailingly follows its doer.

questions.question: True or False: 'अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का' — अतिदर्पेण लङ्का विनष्टा इति श्लोकः वदति। (The verse says Lanka perished through excessive arrogance.)
questions.explanation: अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का — excess of arrogance destroyed Lanka; the verse then warns against all excess.

questions.question: True or False: 'पतन्ति' इति क्रियापदं लृट्लकारे अस्ति। (The verb पतन्ति is in the future tense.)
questions.explanation: पतन्ति is लट्लकार (present tense), third person plural — '(they) fall'. The future would be पतिष्यन्ति.

questions.question: True or False: 'परपीडकः' इति पदं बहुव्रीहिसमासः अस्ति। (The word परपीडकः is a bahuvrihi compound.)
questions.explanation: परपीडकः = परेषां पीडकः is a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष (genitive tatpurusha), not a bahuvrihi.

questions.question: True or False: अध्यायानुसारं कर्कटकस्य कृत्यम् आत्मरक्षा आसीत्, अतः सः परपीडकः न। (According to the chapter, the crab's act was self-defence, so he is not a parapidaka.)
questions.explanation: The crab struck only to save his own life from imminent destruction; self-defence is not tormenting others.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — पतन्ति ______। (Complete the chapter's title.)
questions.explanation: The title is पतन्ति परपीडकाः — 'those who torment others fall'.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय ______। (Complete the verse-line.)
questions.explanation: Vyasa's line: परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् — helping others leads to merit, tormenting them to sin.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — अहिंसा परमो ______। (Complete the verse-line.)
questions.explanation: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-injury is the highest dharma.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — वृद्धः बकः मत्स्यान् ग्रहीतुम् ______ अभवत्। (Fill in the correct Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: The old heron became unable (असमर्थः) to catch fish because of the weakness of old age.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — कर्कटकः शिलायाम् ______ दृष्ट्वा सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् अवगतवान्। (Fill in the correct Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: Seeing the heap of bones (अस्थिराशिम्, accusative) on the rock, the crab understood everything.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — अतिलौल्याद् बकः कश्चिद् मृतः ______। (Complete the verse-line.)
questions.explanation: The verse ends: मृतः कर्कटकग्रहात् — he died from the grip of the crab.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति ______। (Complete the verse-line.)
questions.explanation: The calf finds its mother (मातरम्) even among a thousand cows.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — तथा पूर्वकृतं कर्म ______ अनुगच्छति। (Complete the verse-line.)
questions.explanation: A deed done in the past follows its doer (कर्तारम्).

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — अतिदाने ______ बद्धः। (Complete the verse-line with the right name.)
questions.explanation: अतिदाने बलिर्बद्धः — through excess of giving King Bali was bound.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं पूरयत — तथाहिंसा = तथा + ______। (Complete the sandhi-split.)
questions.explanation: तथा + अहिंसा = तथाहिंसा by दीर्घसन्धि (आ + अ = आ).

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — बकः जलचरेभ्यः ______ आगमनस्य मिथ्याभयम् अदर्शयत्। (Fill in: the heron showed the creatures the false fear of whose coming?)
questions.explanation: He frightened them with the coming of the fishermen (धीवराणाम् आगमनम्) — a pure invention.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — कर्कटकः दंष्ट्राभ्यां ______ ग्रीवां दृढं गृहीतवान्। (Fill in the correct Sanskrit word.)
questions.explanation: He gripped the neck OF THE HERON (बकस्य, genitive) firmly with his pincers.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — आपत्काले ______ एव बलम्। (Complete the crab's watchword.)
questions.explanation: आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम् — in times of danger, courage alone is strength.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — 'अहिंसा' इति पदे ______ समासः अस्ति। (Name the compound in अहिंसा.)
questions.explanation: अहिंसा = न हिंसा — formed with the negative particle नञ्, hence a नञ्समास.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — अति सर्वत्र ______। (Complete the verse-line.)
questions.explanation: अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् — one should avoid excess everywhere.

questions.question: 'पतन्ति परपीडकाः' इति शीर्षकस्य अर्थं लिखत, पदद्वयस्य व्याकरणं च सूचयत। (Write the meaning of the title and note the grammar of its two words.)
questions.answer: The title means 'those who torment others fall/perish'. पतन्ति is लट्लकार, प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन of the root पत् ('to fall'); परपीडकाः is nominative plural of परपीडकः (परेषां पीडकः, षष्ठीतत्पुरुष) — 'tormentors of others'. Together they declare the law that oppressors are destroyed.
questions.explanation: The title itself is a complete Sanskrit sentence — verb + subject.

questions.question: बकः शोकं किमर्थम् अनाटयत्? (Why did the heron act out grief on the bank of the lake?)
questions.answer: Being too weak with old age to catch fish by strength, the heron decided to live by trickery. He shed false tears and acted grief-stricken so that the curious fish would approach and ask the reason — giving him the chance to tell his lie about the fishermen and win their trust.
questions.explanation: The feigned grief was the first step of his stratagem (उपाय) to bring the fish to him.

questions.question: बकः जलचरेभ्यः किं मिथ्यावचनम् अवदत्? किं च प्रत्यजानात्? (What lie did the heron tell the water-creatures, and what did he promise?)
questions.answer: He lied that fishermen would come the next day, cast their nets and kill all the water-creatures of the lake. He then promised to carry them one by one (एकैकशः) to a vast, clear lake nearby where there was no fear of fishermen.
questions.explanation: The false threat created fear; the false promise created trust — the two tools of the deceiver.

questions.question: कर्कटकः बकस्य कपटं कथम् अवगतवान्? (How did the crab discover the heron's deceit?)
questions.answer: While being carried through the air, the crab looked down as they neared the rock and saw the great heap of fish-bones (अस्थिराशिः) lying on it. From this he understood that the heron had never carried anyone to a new lake but had eaten every fish there — and that his own turn had now come.
questions.explanation: Observation (सूक्ष्मदृष्टि) revealed the truth that blind trust had hidden.

questions.question: कर्कटकस्य बकहननम् अहिंसा-सिद्धान्तस्य विरुद्धं न मन्यते — किमर्थम्? सयुक्तिकम् उत्तरत। (Why is the crab's killing of the heron not considered contrary to the principle of ahimsa? Answer with reasons.)
questions.answer: Ahimsa forbids aggression — the wanton tormenting of others — but it does not demand that an innocent creature surrender to slaughter. The crab did not attack first, gained nothing by cruelty, and struck only when his destruction was certain and no other escape existed. His act was आत्मरक्षा (self-defence) against an aggressor, which the tradition distinguishes from परपीडन (tormenting others). The blame for the violence rests on the aggressor heron, whose own cruelty created the situation.
questions.explanation: The chapter contrasts the heron's aggressive himsa with the crab's defensive act — only the former is परपीडनम्.

questions.question: अधोलिखितानां पदानां शब्दार्थं लिखत — सरः, धीवरः, शिला, ग्रीवा, दंष्ट्रा। (Write the English meanings of these words.)
questions.answer: सरः = lake; धीवरः = fisherman; शिला = rock; ग्रीवा = neck; दंष्ट्रा = pincer/claw (literally fang).
questions.explanation: All five words are central to the story: the lake, the invented fishermen, the rock of bones, and the neck gripped by the pincers.

questions.question: 'अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम्...' इति श्लोकस्य अन्वयं कृत्वा अर्थं लिखत। (Give the anvaya and meaning of the verse.)
questions.answer: अन्वयः: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् (अस्ति) — परोपकारः पुण्याय (भवति), परपीडनम् पापाय (भवति)। Meaning: In all the eighteen Puranas Vyasa's teaching comes down to two sayings — doing good to others leads to merit, and tormenting others leads to sin. The whole of dharma is condensed into this one contrast.
questions.explanation: पुण्याय and पापाय are datives of purpose/result (तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी).

questions.question: 'अहिंसा परमो धर्मः...' इति श्लोकं व्याख्यात — अहिंसा केषां चतुर्णां परमा उच्यते? (Explain the ahimsa verse — of which four things is ahimsa called the highest?)
questions.answer: The verse declares ahimsa the highest of four things: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः (the highest righteousness), तथा अहिंसा परो दमः (the highest self-control), अहिंसा परमं दानम् (the highest charity), and अहिंसा परमं तपः (the highest austerity). Non-injury is thus not one virtue among many but the crown of all virtue — refraining from harm is itself dharma, discipline, gift and penance.
questions.explanation: The four-fold repetition drives home that every path of virtue culminates in non-injury.

questions.question: 'यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम्...' — श्लोकस्य उपमां तात्पर्यं च स्पष्टीकुरुत। (Explain the simile and purport of the verse.)
questions.answer: The simile: just as a calf let loose among a thousand cows unerringly finds its own mother, so a deed done in the past (पूर्वकृतं कर्म) finds and follows its doer (कर्तारम् अनुगच्छति). The purport: karma never loses its way or its target; however long the delay or however far the flight, the fruit of one's own action arrives. The heron's cruelty found him in mid-air, far from the lake.
questions.explanation: The mother-calf bond stands for the unbreakable link between doer and deed.

questions.question: 'अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का...' श्लोके त्रीणि उदाहरणानि कानि? तेषां सामान्यः उपदेशः कः? (What are the three examples in the verse, and what common lesson do they teach?)
questions.answer: The three examples: (i) अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का — Lanka (Ravana's city) was destroyed through excess of arrogance; (ii) अतिमाने च कौरवाः — the Kauravas perished through excess of pride; (iii) अतिदाने बलिर्बद्धः — King Bali was bound through excess even of giving. Common lesson: अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् — excess of anything, even of a virtue like charity, leads to downfall; one should practise moderation everywhere.
questions.explanation: Two examples are of vices in excess, the third shows even a virtue in excess brings a fall — making the warning universal.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कृत्वा सन्धेः नाम लिखत — (i) धर्मस्तथाहिंसा (ii) बलिर्बद्धः (iii) नास्ति। (Split each form and name the sandhi.)
questions.answer: (i) धर्मस्तथाहिंसा = धर्मः + तथा + अहिंसा — विसर्गसन्धि (ः → स् before त) and दीर्घसन्धि (आ + अ = आ). (ii) बलिर्बद्धः = बलिः + बद्धः — विसर्गसन्धि (visarga → र् before a voiced consonant). (iii) नास्ति = न + अस्ति — दीर्घसन्धि (अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: All three joined forms occur in the chapter's verses and prose.

questions.question: समास-विग्रहं कृत्वा समासस्य नाम लिखत — (i) परपीडकः (ii) परोपकारः (iii) अस्थिराशिः। (Give the vigraha and name of each compound.)
questions.answer: (i) परपीडकः = परेषां पीडकः — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः ('tormentor of others'). (ii) परोपकारः = परेषाम् उपकारः — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः ('help to others'). (iii) अस्थिराशिः = अस्थ्नां राशिः — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः ('heap of bones').
questions.explanation: All three are genitive tatpurusha compounds; the first member stands in the genitive relation to the second.

questions.question: अधोलिखितानां क्रियापदानां लकारं लिखत — आगमिष्यन्ति, अपतत्, पतन्ति, वर्जयेत्। (State the lakara of each verb.)
questions.answer: आगमिष्यन्ति — लृट्लकारः (future, 'they will come'); अपतत् — लङ्लकारः (past, 'he fell'); पतन्ति — लट्लकारः (present, 'they fall'); वर्जयेत् — विधिलिङ् (optative, 'one should avoid').
questions.explanation: The four verbs illustrate the chapter's four lakaras: लृट्, लङ्, लट् and विधिलिङ्.

questions.question: अधोलिखितानां पदानां विभक्तिं वचनं च लिखत — सरसि, वार्धक्येन, बकस्य, ग्रीवाम्। (State the vibhakti and number of each word.)
questions.answer: सरसि — सप्तमी विभक्तिः, एकवचनम् ('in the lake'); वार्धक्येन — तृतीया, एकवचनम् ('by/because of old age'); बकस्य — षष्ठी, एकवचनम् ('of the heron'); ग्रीवाम् — द्वितीया, एकवचनम् ('the neck', object).
questions.explanation: Locative, instrumental of cause, genitive and accusative — four core case-roles from the story.

questions.question: अनुवादं कुरुत — 'ततः कर्कटकः शनैः शनैः स्वसरः प्रत्यागत्य सर्वं वृत्तान्तं जलचरेभ्यः न्यवेदयत्।' (Translate into English.)
questions.answer: 'Then the crab, slowly making his way back to his own lake, reported the whole account to the water-creatures.' — ततः = then; शनैः शनैः = slowly; स्वसरः प्रत्यागत्य = having returned to his own lake; सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् = the whole account; जलचरेभ्यः न्यवेदयत् = reported to the water-creatures.
questions.explanation: प्रत्यागत्य is the gerund 'having returned'; जलचरेभ्यः is the dative of the recipients of the report.

questions.question: अनुवादं कुरुत — 'धीवराः श्वः अत्र आगमिष्यन्ति, जालानि क्षेप्स्यन्ति, सर्वान् जलचरान् मारयिष्यन्ति।' (Translate into English.)
questions.answer: 'Fishermen will come here tomorrow, they will cast (their) nets, and they will kill all the water-creatures.' — धीवराः = fishermen; श्वः = tomorrow; जालानि क्षेप्स्यन्ति = will cast nets; सर्वान् जलचरान् मारयिष्यन्ति = will kill all the water-creatures.
questions.explanation: All three verbs are लृट् (future) third person plural — the grammar of the heron's invented threat.

questions.question: मत्स्याः बकस्य वचने किमर्थं विश्वासं कृतवन्तः? अस्मात् कः पाठः ग्राह्यः? (Why did the fish trust the heron's words? What lesson should be drawn?)
questions.answer: The fish were seized by fear at the news of the fishermen and, desperate for safety, took refuge in the very creature who had always been their predator. They tested nothing — no one followed the heron or asked for proof of the new lake. The lesson: fear destroys judgement, and sweet words are not evidence. Before trusting, one must verify (परीक्ष्य विश्वसेत्); blind trust in the wicked delivers the trusting to destruction.
questions.explanation: The story blames not trust itself but unverified trust born of panic.

questions.question: कर्कटकस्य चरित्रचित्रणं त्रिषु चतुर्षु वा वाक्येषु कुरुत। (Sketch the character of the crab in three or four sentences.)
questions.answer: The crab is observant: alone among the creatures he looked down and read the meaning of the bone-heap. He is composed in crisis — even facing certain death he told himself आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम् and did not panic. He is decisive and brave, gripping the aggressor's neck at the right moment, and he is responsible: he returned to warn the community and report the truth. He embodies presence of mind joined to courage.
questions.explanation: Observation, composure, decisiveness and social responsibility are the four traits the story gives the crab.

questions.question: कथायाम् अस्थिराशिः कस्य प्रतीकः? (What does the heap of bones symbolise in the story?)
questions.answer: The bone-heap is the accumulated, undeniable record of the oppressor's crimes. Every act of cruelty left its trace, and though the heron hid his deeds from the lake, the evidence piled up at the scene until a single observant victim read it. It symbolises the truth that wrongdoing cannot be hidden forever — the oppressor's own past exposes and destroys him.
questions.explanation: The symbol links the story to the karma verse: the deeds themselves wait to testify against the doer.

questions.question: 'अतिलौल्यम्' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? बकस्य मृत्यौ तस्य का भूमिका? (What does अतिलौल्यम् mean, and what role did it play in the heron's death?)
questions.answer: अतिलौल्यम् means excessive greed or over-craving (अति + लौल्य). Not content with devouring all the fish, the heron craved a new taste and carried the crab — the one creature armed with pincers — placing him on his own neck. His greed thus put the instrument of his death at his throat: अतिलौल्याद् बकः मृतः कर्कटकग्रहात्.
questions.explanation: Greed blinded the heron to the danger; the verse names अतिलौल्य as the very cause of his death.

questions.question: 'आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम्' — अनुवादं कृत्वा एकवाक्येन टिप्पणीं लिखत। (Translate and comment in one sentence.)
questions.answer: Translation: 'In the time of danger, courage alone is strength.' Comment: the crab proves the maxim — with no physical match for the flying heron, his refusal to panic and his presence of mind became the strength that saved his life and destroyed the oppressor.
questions.explanation: The maxim is the crab's thought at the moment he saw the bone-heap.

questions.question: परोपकारः परपीडनं च — अनयोः भेदं सोदाहरणं स्पष्टीकुरुत। (Distinguish between paropakara and parapidana with one example of each.)
questions.answer: परोपकारः (परेषाम् उपकारः) is acting for the good of others — e.g. a person who genuinely carries stranded creatures to safety, or one who feeds the hungry; the verse says it leads to पुण्य (merit). परपीडनम् is causing pain to others for one's own gain — e.g. the heron, who used a false promise of rescue to devour the trusting fish; the verse says it leads to पाप (sin). The same outward act (carrying creatures to 'safety') becomes opposite in moral value according to the intention and the result.
questions.explanation: The story deliberately dresses परपीडन in the costume of परोपकार to teach that intention, not appearance, decides which is which.

questions.question: बक-कर्कट-कथां स्वभाषया विस्तरेण लिखत, अन्ते नीतिं च स्पष्टीकुरुत। (Narrate the heron-and-crab story in detail in your own words, and state its moral at the end.)
questions.answer: Model answer: By a great forest lake lived an old heron, too weak with age to catch fish. Choosing trickery over strength, he stood on the bank shedding false tears. When a fish asked the reason, he claimed fishermen would come the next day, cast nets and kill every water-creature, and — feigning compassion — offered to carry them one by one to a vast, safe lake nearby. The frightened creatures trusted him. Daily he flew a few fish to a huge rock and devoured them, until a great heap of bones covered it. One day the crab asked to be taken; the heron, craving a new taste, placed him on his neck and flew toward the rock. Looking down, the crab saw the bone-heap and understood everything. Refusing to panic — 'in danger, courage alone is strength' — he gripped the heron's neck with his sharp pincers and squeezed until the wicked bird died and fell to earth. The crab returned and told the creatures all; they praised him and became fearless. Moral: पतन्ति परपीडकाः — he who torments and deceives others is destroyed by his own cruelty; observation and courage protect the innocent.
questions.explanation: A complete narration covers the deceit, the daily betrayal, the discovery, the counter-stroke and the return, ending with the explicit moral.

questions.question: 'पतन्ति परपीडकाः' इति शीर्षकं कथायाः कृते सर्वथा उचितम् — इति कथनं कथाघटनाभिः समर्थयत। (Justify with events from the story that the title is entirely apt for this tale.)
questions.answer: Model answer: The title states a law — tormentors of others fall — and every movement of the story proves it. First, the heron's oppression is deliberate: he manufactures fear with the fishermen-lie, poses as a rescuer, and betrays absolute trust by devouring his wards one by one; he is परपीडक in the fullest sense. Second, his fall is produced by his own deeds, not by chance: the bone-heap — the record of his crimes — is what exposes him, and his greed for crab-flesh is what places the armed victim at his throat. Third, the agent of his fall is one of his intended victims acting in self-defence, showing that oppression itself breeds its destroyer. Finally, the aftermath completes the title: with the oppressor fallen, the lake becomes fearless. The verse भक्षयित्वा बहून् मत्स्यान्... seals the same judgement: अतिलौल्याद् बकः मृतः कर्कटकग्रहात्. The title is thus not a mere label but the story's thesis, demonstrated step by step.
questions.explanation: Full marks require linking the title's claim to specific events: the deceit, the bone-heap, the greed, the victim-turned-destroyer and the fearless aftermath.

questions.question: अध्यायस्य पञ्चसु नीतिश्लोकेषु कर्मसिद्धान्तः अहिंसा च कथं प्रतिपादिते? विस्तरेण विश्लेषयत। (How do the five verses of the chapter expound the law of karma and ahimsa? Analyse in detail.)
questions.answer: Model answer: The verses form a single moral argument. (1) Vyasa's couplet gives the foundation: परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् — all merit flows from helping, all sin from harming; karma begins with this two-fold seed. (2) The ahimsa verse raises non-injury to the summit of four paths — dharma, self-control, charity, austerity — so that harming others becomes the deepest possible wrong. (3) The heron-verse supplies the case-study: अतिलौल्याद् बकः मृतः कर्कटकग्रहात् — greed-driven cruelty ripened, within the story itself, into the doer's death. (4) The calf-and-mother verse states the mechanism: as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारम् अनुगच्छति — the deed never misses its doer; delay is not escape. (5) The excess-verse universalises the warning: arrogance destroyed Lanka, pride the Kauravas, and even unmeasured giving bound Bali — अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्. Together: practise ahimsa and paropakara, for the law of karma guarantees that harm returns to the harmer — the doctrinal ground of पतन्ति परपीडकाः.
questions.explanation: The analysis should show the progression: principle → supreme value → example → mechanism → universal warning.

questions.question: अध्यायात् उदाहरणानि गृहीत्वा सन्धेः समासस्य च त्रीन् त्रीन् भेदान् सविग्रहं सोदाहरणं व्याख्यात। (Taking examples from the chapter, explain three kinds of sandhi and three kinds of samasa with analysis.)
questions.answer: Model answer: SANDHI — (1) दीर्घसन्धिः: like vowels merge into one long vowel — तथा + अहिंसा = तथाहिंसा (आ+अ=आ); न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ+अ=आ). (2) विसर्गसन्धिः: the visarga changes by its neighbour — धर्मः + तथा = धर्मस्तथा (ः→स् before त); बलिः + बद्धः = बलिर्बद्धः (ः→र् before a voiced consonant). (3) यण्सन्धिः: इ/उ before an unlike vowel become य्/व् — प्रति + आगत्य = प्रत्यागत्य (इ+आ=या). SAMASA — (1) षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः: first member in genitive relation — परपीडकः = परेषां पीडकः; परोपकारः = परेषाम् उपकारः; अस्थिराशिः = अस्थ्नां राशिः. (2) उपपदसमासः: a verbal element as final member — जलचरः = जले चरति इति ('what moves in water'). (3) नञ्समासः: negative particle compounded — अहिंसा = न हिंसा ('non-injury'). Each analysed form occurs in the chapter's own prose or verses.
questions.explanation: Marks for correctly naming each type, splitting/analysing the form, and drawing every example from the chapter.

questions.question: लट्-लङ्-लृट्-विधिलिङ् इति चतुर्णां लकाराणां प्रयोगम् अध्यायस्य क्रियापदैः सोदाहरणं व्याख्यात। (Explain the use of the four lakaras with verb examples from the chapter.)
questions.answer: Model answer: (1) लट् (present tense) states what is happening or what is always true: पतन्ति परपीडकाः 'oppressors fall' (a universal law), विन्दति 'finds', अनुगच्छति 'follows', शोचामि 'I grieve'. (2) लङ् (past tense) narrates completed events, marked by the augment अ-: अवदत् 'he said', अपृच्छत् 'he asked', अपीडयत् 'he squeezed', अपतत् 'he fell', न्यवेदयत् 'he reported'. (3) लृट् (simple future) with the -स्य/इष्य- marker expresses what will happen: आगमिष्यन्ति 'they will come', क्षेप्स्यन्ति 'they will cast', मारयिष्यन्ति 'they will kill', नेष्यामि 'I shall carry', खादिष्यामि 'I shall eat'. (4) विधिलिङ् (optative/potential) expresses 'should/ought' — advice or possibility: वर्जयेत् 'one should avoid (excess)', भवेत् 'it may/should be'. In the story the heron's lie lives in लृट् (threats and promises about tomorrow), the narration in लङ्, the morals in लट् and विधिलिङ् — tense itself mirrors the tale's structure.
questions.explanation: Marks for naming each lakara's sense, giving chapter verbs for each, and noting person/number where relevant.

questions.question: 'पतन्ति परपीडकाः' इति सिद्धान्तः आधुनिकजीवने कथं दृश्यते? द्वे त्रीणि वा उदाहरणानि दत्त्वा पाठस्य उपदेशं वर्तमानसन्दर्भे लिखत। (How is the principle seen in modern life? Give two or three examples and state the chapter's teaching in a present-day context.)
questions.answer: Model answer: The heron's method — manufacture fear, pose as the rescuer, devour the trusting — recurs constantly today. (1) Financial fraud: a schemer warns people their savings are unsafe and promises a 'secure' scheme, then disappears with the deposits; like the heron he is undone when the record of victims (the bone-heap) surfaces and one alert investor exposes him. (2) Bullying and harassment: one who repeatedly torments juniors or subordinates loses their trust, and a single documented complaint brings the fall. (3) Exploitative moneylending or cyber-scams follow the same arc — concealed cruelty accumulates evidence until it destroys the doer. The chapter's teaching for today: never trust sweet words without verification (the fishes' error); keep observation and courage in crisis (the crab's strength); and remember that wrongdoing is self-defeating — कर्म कर्तारम् अनुगच्छति, and those who torment others fall.
questions.explanation: Any reasonable modern examples earn marks if they map the heron's pattern (false fear, false rescue, hidden harm, eventual exposure) and end with the stated lesson.

questions.question: अनुवादं कुरुत — 'शिलायाः समीपं गत्वा कर्कटकः अधः अपश्यत्। तत्र अस्थिराशिं दृष्ट्वा सः सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् अवगतवान्। ... सः स्वतीक्ष्णाभ्यां दंष्ट्राभ्यां बकस्य ग्रीवां दृढं गृहीत्वा अपीडयत्। दुष्टः बकः प्राणान् अत्यजत्, भूमौ च अपतत्।' अन्ते द्वित्रैः वाक्यैः अंशस्य महत्त्वं लिखत। (Translate the climax passage and add two or three sentences on its significance.)
questions.answer: Model answer — Translation: 'Going near the rock, the crab looked down. Seeing the heap of bones there, he understood the whole affair. ... He gripped the heron's neck firmly with his two sharp pincers and squeezed. The wicked heron gave up his life-breaths and fell to the earth.' Significance: This is the turning point where hidden cruelty meets its fruit — the evidence of the heron's crimes (the bone-heap) itself triggers his destruction. The verb अपतत् ('he fell') physically enacts the title पतन्ति परपीडकाः: the oppressor literally falls. And the fall comes through the very victim he carried at his own neck, showing that the tormentor carries his destroyer with him.
questions.explanation: Marks for accurate rendering of the gerunds (गत्वा, दृष्ट्वा, गृहीत्वा), the instrumental दंष्ट्राभ्याम्, and the concluding comment tying अपतत् to the title.

questions.question: बकस्य कर्कटकस्य च चरित्रयोः तुलनां कुरुत — कौ गुणौ कौ दोषौ च कथा प्रदर्शयति? (Compare the characters of the heron and the crab — what virtues and vices does the story display through them?)
questions.answer: Model answer: The two characters are moral opposites. The heron: intelligent but his intelligence serves cruelty — he converts weakness into weaponised deceit; his vices are कपट (deception), हिंसा (cruelty to the trusting), कृतघ्नता toward those who called him 'uncle' and protector, and अतिलौल्य (insatiable greed), which finally blinds him. The crab: equally intelligent, but his intelligence serves truth and life — सूक्ष्मदृष्टि (he alone observes the bone-heap), विवेक (he reads its meaning instantly), धैर्य (he does not panic in mid-air: आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम्), साहस (he strikes at the decisive moment, and only in self-defence), and सामाजिकं दायित्वम् (he returns to warn the community). The story's point: intellect is morally neutral — joined to cruelty it digs the doer's grave; joined to courage and dharma it protects life. The heron falls by his vices; the crab is honoured for his virtues.
questions.explanation: A full comparison names paired qualities — deceit vs observation, greed vs restraint, cruelty vs self-defence, secrecy vs responsibility.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'ततः सः बकः सरसः तीरे स्थित्वा अश्रूणि मुञ्चन् शोकं नाटयति स्म। तं दुःखितं दृष्ट्वा एकः मत्स्यः अपृच्छत् — मातुल! किमर्थम् अद्य आहारं न करोषि? किमर्थं च रोदिषि?'
(i) बकः किं नाटयति स्म? (ii) मत्स्यः बकं केन सम्बोधनेन आहूतवान्? (iii) 'अश्रूणि' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (iv) Translate: 'तं दुःखितं दृष्ट्वा एकः मत्स्यः अपृच्छत्।'
questions.answer: (i) बकः शोकं नाटयति स्म — he was acting out grief, shedding false tears. (ii) 'मातुल!' (uncle) इति सम्बोधनेन — a term of trust and respect. (iii) अश्रूणि = tears (अश्रु, neuter plural). (iv) 'Seeing him sorrowful, a fish asked (him).'
questions.explanation: The passage shows the first step of the deceit: feigned grief designed to draw the trusting fish close.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'ततः प्रभृति सः बकः प्रतिदिनं कांश्चित् मत्स्यान् चञ्च्वा गृहीत्वा उड्डयते स्म, किन्तु नूतनं सरः न नयति स्म। सः एकां विशालां शिलाम् उपगम्य तत्र तान् निर्दयं खादति स्म।'
(i) बकः मत्स्यान् केन गृहीत्वा उड्डयते स्म? (ii) सः तान् कुत्र खादति स्म? (iii) 'निर्दयम्' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (iv) अंशः बकस्य कं स्वभावं प्रकटयति?
questions.answer: (i) चञ्च्वा — with his beak (तृतीया एकवचन of चञ्चुः). (ii) विशालां शिलाम् उपगम्य तत्र — on reaching a huge rock, he ate them there. (iii) निर्दयम् = pitilessly, without mercy. (iv) The passage exposes his systematic cruelty and treachery — a daily, deliberate betrayal of creatures who trusted him as their rescuer.
questions.explanation: The daily routine of betrayal shows the heron's cruelty was planned and habitual, not a single lapse.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'कर्कटकः अधः अपश्यत्। तत्र अस्थिराशिं दृष्ट्वा सः सर्वं वृत्तान्तम् अवगतवान् — अयं धूर्तः सर्वान् मत्स्यान् भक्षितवान्। अधुना मम अपि विनाशकालः समागतः। तथापि धैर्यं न त्यजामि।'
(i) कर्कटकः अधः किम् अपश्यत्? (ii) 'धूर्तः' इति केन विषये उक्तम्? (iii) कर्कटकः किं न त्यजामि इति निश्चितवान्? (iv) Translate: 'अधुना मम अपि विनाशकालः समागतः।'
questions.answer: (i) सः अधः अस्थिराशिम् अपश्यत् — he saw the heap of bones below. (ii) बकस्य विषये — the crab calls the heron a rogue (धूर्तः). (iii) धैर्यम् — he resolved not to abandon courage. (iv) 'Now my hour of destruction too has arrived.'
questions.explanation: The crab's inner monologue joins discovery, danger and resolve — the hinge of the whole story.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् ।
परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् ॥'
(i) वचनद्वयं कस्य? (ii) पुण्याय किं भवति? (iii) 'वचनद्वयम्' इत्यस्य समास-विग्रहं कुरुत। (iv) 'पापाय' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.answer: (i) व्यासस्य — the pair of sayings is Vyasa's. (ii) परोपकारः पुण्याय भवति — helping others leads to merit. (iii) वचनद्वयम् = वचनयोः द्वयम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः) — 'a pair of sayings'. (iv) चतुर्थी विभक्तिः (तादर्थ्ये — dative of purpose/result).
questions.explanation: The verse condenses all the Puranas into one contrast; its datives पुण्याय/पापाय express result.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'अहिंसा परमो धर्मस्तथाहिंसा परो दमः ।
अहिंसा परमं दानम् अहिंसा परमं तपः ॥'
(i) परमो धर्मः कः? (ii) 'धर्मस्तथाहिंसा' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत। (iii) 'अहिंसा' इति पदे कः समासः? (iv) श्लोकस्य केन्द्रीयः उपदेशः कः?
questions.answer: (i) अहिंसा — non-injury is the highest dharma. (ii) धर्मस्तथाहिंसा = धर्मः + तथा + अहिंसा (विसर्गसन्धि and दीर्घसन्धि). (iii) नञ्समासः — अहिंसा = न हिंसा. (iv) The central teaching: non-injury is supreme in every domain — it is at once the highest righteousness, self-control, charity and austerity.
questions.explanation: One verse, four superlatives — ahimsa crowns dharma, dama, dana and tapas alike.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'भक्षयित्वा बहून् मत्स्यान् उत्तमाधममध्यमान् ।
अतिलौल्याद् बकः कश्चिद् मृतः कर्कटकग्रहात् ॥'
(i) बकः कान् भक्षितवान्? (ii) सः कस्मात् कारणात् मृतः? (iii) 'भक्षयित्वा' इति पदं किं सूचयति (कृदन्तभेदः)? (iv) श्लोकः कथायाः केन अंशेन सम्बद्धः?
questions.answer: (i) उत्तमाधममध्यमान् बहून् मत्स्यान् — many fish of every grade: best, worst and middling. (ii) अतिलौल्यात् — from excessive greed, (dying) कर्कटकग्रहात् in the crab's grip. (iii) भक्षयित्वा is a क्त्वान्त (gerund/absolutive) — 'having devoured', showing the action completed before his death. (iv) It is the traditional summary-verse of the whole tale — the heron's career of devouring and his death by the crab.
questions.explanation: The verse compresses the entire fable into two lines: the crime (devouring), the flaw (greed) and the fall (the crab's grip).

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् ।
तथा पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारमनुगच्छति ॥'
(i) वत्सः कां विन्दति? (ii) कर्म कम् अनुगच्छति? (iii) 'धेनुसहस्रेषु' इति पदे का विभक्तिः किं वचनम्? (iv) श्लोकः बकस्य कथायां कथं घटते?
questions.answer: (i) मातरम् — the calf finds its own mother. (ii) कर्तारम् — the deed follows its doer. (iii) सप्तमी विभक्तिः, बहुवचनम् ('among a thousand cows'). (iv) The heron's past cruelty followed him like the calf its mother: the bones of his victims and his own greed found him out mid-air, and his deed returned as death in the crab's grip.
questions.explanation: The verse gives the mechanism of the story's justice — karma unerringly reaches the doer.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'अतिदर्पे हता लङ्का अतिमाने च कौरवाः ।
अतिदाने बलिर्बद्धो ह्यति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् ॥'
(i) लङ्का केन हता? (ii) कौरवाः केन (हताः)? (iii) 'बलिर्बद्धः' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत। (iv) श्लोकस्य उपदेशं बकस्य अतिलौल्येन सह योजयत।
questions.answer: (i) अतिदर्पेण — by excessive arrogance. (ii) अतिमानेन — by excessive pride. (iii) बलिर्बद्धः = बलिः + बद्धः (विसर्गसन्धिः — visarga becomes र् before a voiced consonant). (iv) The verse warns that every excess destroys — pride destroyed Lanka and the Kauravas, and even excessive giving bound Bali; the heron's अतिलौल्य (excess of greed) belongs to the same list: not content with the fish, he craved the crab and thereby carried his own death to his neck.
questions.explanation: The chapter's fable is one more entry in the verse's catalogue of falls caused by excess.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer the questions —
A stranger arrives in a village and warns the people that their bank will collapse within a week. He offers to 'protect' their savings in his own 'safe scheme', collecting deposits from trusting families one by one. One villager, before depositing, quietly checks the scheme's records and finds a list of earlier victims in another district. She alerts the police, and the fraudster is arrested with the villagers' money recovered.
(i) Which character of the chapter does the stranger correspond to, and why? (ii) Which character does the alert villager correspond to? (iii) Which two elements of the heron's method appear in the stranger's plan? (iv) Which maxim of the chapter does the villager's action illustrate?
questions.answer: (i) The heron (बकः) — like him, the stranger manufactures a false danger and poses as the rescuer in order to devour the trusting. (ii) The crab (कर्कटकः) — she observes, verifies and acts, saving herself and the community. (iii) The false threat (fishermen/bank collapse) to create fear, and the false promise of safety (new lake/safe scheme) to win trust; the 'list of earlier victims' parallels the heap of bones. (iv) आपत्काले धैर्यम् एव बलम् together with the chapter's law पतन्ति परपीडकाः — verification and courage expose the oppressor, and the tormentor falls by the record of his own deeds.
questions.explanation: The case maps the fable onto modern financial fraud: threat, false rescue, hidden victims, alert observer, downfall.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं वाक्यं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'धीवराः श्वः अत्र आगमिष्यन्ति, जालानि क्षेप्स्यन्ति, सर्वान् जलचरान् मारयिष्यन्ति।'
(i) 'आगमिष्यन्ति' इति पदे कः लकारः? (ii) 'जालानि' इति पदे का विभक्तिः किं वचनम्? (iii) 'जलचरान्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (iv) वाक्ये त्रयाणां क्रियापदानाम् एकः एव लकारः — किं तात्पर्यम्?
questions.answer: (i) लृट्लकारः (simple future). (ii) द्वितीया विभक्तिः, बहुवचनम् — 'nets' as the object of क्षेप्स्यन्ति (जाल is neuter, so the form is जालानि). (iii) द्वितीया विभक्तिः, बहुवचनम् — object of मारयिष्यन्ति. (iv) All three verbs are लृट् because the entire threat lies in the future — the heron frightens the creatures with what 'will' happen tomorrow; the future tense is the very grammar of his lie.
questions.explanation: The sentence is a grammar capsule: three future verbs with their accusative objects, serving the story's deceit.
